links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM clinical outputs when all cases were re-queried one month later
links.effect: All three LLMs showed almost perfect clinical stability (Cronbach's α = 0.831-0.856); feedback did not significantly reduce misdiagnosis rates in subsequent interactions.
links.quote: All LLMs demonstrated an almost perfect clinical stability (α = 0.831-0.856), though human feedback did not significantly reduce misdiagnosis rates in subsequent interactions.

unlisted_practices: Feeding identified errors back to the LLM and re-querying to test short-term correctability (did not improve accuracy)
Comparing pharmacovigilance information quality across LLMs using blinded pharmacist ratings

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLMs on otolaryngology clinical vignettes and tests whether feeding back clinician-identified errors to models (human feedback/correctability) improves diagnostic accuracy upon re-querying.
